summary: Hashem created the world with ten sayings, even though He could have used one. This shows how much it matters: the wicked who ruin the world are punished more, and the tzaddikim who keep it going get a bigger reward.

chunks.en: The world was created with ten sayings.
chunks.explain: Ten times the Torah says "And Hashem said" in the story of creation.

chunks.en: And what does this teach us?
Couldn't it have been created with one saying?
But it is to punish the wicked who ruin
the world that was created with ten sayings,
and to give a good reward to the tzaddikim who keep up
the world that was created with ten sayings.

summary: There were ten generations from Adam to Noach, and ten from Noach to Avraham. This shows how patient Hashem is. Avraham came and got the reward of all of them.

chunks.en: There were ten generations from Adam until Noach,
to show how patient Hashem is,

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת הָיוּ מַכְעִיסִין וּבָאִין עַד
chunks.en: because all the generations kept making Him angry, until
He brought the waters of the Flood on them.
There were ten generations from Noach until Avraham,
to show how patient Hashem is,
because all the generations kept making Him angry,
until Avraham came and took
for himself the reward of all of them.

summary: Avraham Avinu was tested ten times and passed every test. This shows how much he loved Hashem.

chunks.en: Avraham Avinu was tested with ten tests,
peace be upon him, and he stood strong in all of them,
to show how great the love of
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, was.

summary: Hashem did ten miracles for our fathers in Mitzrayim and ten at the sea, and brought ten makkos on the Mitzrim in Mitzrayim and ten at the sea. Our fathers tested Hashem ten times in the desert.

chunks.en: Ten miracles were done for our fathers
in Mitzrayim, and ten at the sea.

chunks.he: עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
chunks.en: Ten makkos the Holy One, blessed is He, brought

chunks.he: עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים בְּמִצְרַיִם וְעֶשֶׂר עַל הַיָּם.
chunks.en: on the Mitzrim in Mitzrayim, and ten at the sea.
With ten tests our fathers tested
Hashem, blessed is He, ten times in the desert,
as it says (Bamidbar 14): And they tested Me these
ten times and did not listen to My voice.

summary: Ten miracles happened all the time in the Beis HaMikdash. For example, the korban meat never went bad, no fly was seen where the animals were prepared, and there was always room for everyone.

chunks.he: עֲשָׂרָה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
chunks.en: Ten miracles were done for our fathers in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: לֹא הִפִּילָה אִשָּׁה מֵרֵיחַ בְּשַׂר הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
chunks.en: No woman expecting a baby was ever harmed by the smell of the holy meat,
and the holy meat never went bad,
and no fly was seen in the place where the animals were prepared,
and it never happened that the Kohen
Gadol became tamei on Yom Kippur,
and the rain never put out the fire
of the wood on the mizbe'ach,

words.note: The pile of wood on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.he: וְלֹא נָצְחָה הָרוּחַ אֶת עַמּוּד הֶעָשָׁן,
chunks.en: and the wind never pushed away the pillar of smoke,
and nothing was ever found unfit in the Omer,

words.note: The barley offering brought on the second day of Pesach.

chunks.en: or in the Two Breads, or in the Lechem HaPanim.
They stood squeezed together, yet bowed with plenty of room,

chunks.he: וְלֹא הִזִּיק נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם מֵעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: and no snake or scorpion ever hurt anyone in Yerushalayim,
and no person ever said to his friend: There is not
enough room for me to sleep over in Yerushalayim.

summary: Ten special things were created at the very end of the six days of creation, just before the first Shabbos, like the mouth of the earth that swallowed Korach, the mann, and the Luchos.

chunks.en: Ten things were created on Erev
Shabbos at twilight,
and these are they:
the mouth of the earth,
and the mouth of the well,
and the mouth of the donkey,
and the rainbow, and the mann,
and the staff, and the shamir,

words.note: A tiny creature that could cut stone.

chunks.en: and the writing, and the writing tool,
and the Luchos. And some say:
also the harmful spirits,
and Moshe's grave,
and the ram of Avraham Avinu.
And some say:
also the tongs, which are made with tongs.
chunks.explain: Someone had to make the very first tongs.

summary: This mishnah lists seven ways a wise person behaves: he lets someone greater speak first, doesn't interrupt, answers carefully, and admits the truth. A foolish person does the opposite.

chunks.en: There are seven things in a foolish person, and seven in a wise person.
A wise person does not speak before someone
who is greater than him in wisdom and in years,
and he does not break into his friend's words,
and he does not rush to answer,
he asks about the topic and answers according to the halachah,
and he talks about the first thing first
and about the last thing last,
and about what he did not hear,
he says: I did not hear.
And he admits the truth.
And the opposite of these are in the foolish person.

summary: Seven kinds of punishment come to the world for seven kinds of aveiros. For example, when people don't give maaser, there is hunger.

chunks.en: Seven kinds of punishments come to the world
for seven main kinds of aveirah.
When some give maaser and some do not give maaser,
a hunger of dryness comes,
some are hungry and some are full.
When they decided not to give maaser,

chunks.he: רָעָב שֶׁל מְהוּמָה וְשֶׁל בַּצֹּרֶת בָּאָה.
chunks.en: a hunger of confusion and of dryness comes.
And when they decided not to take challah,

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: a hunger that destroys comes.

chunks.he: דֶּבֶר בָּא לָעוֹלָם עַל מִיתוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת
chunks.en: A plague comes to the world for deaths said
in the Torah that were not given to beis din,
and for the fruits of Shemittah.
chunks.explain: Using the fruit of the seventh year the wrong way.

chunks.he: חֶרֶב בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם עַל עִנּוּי הַדִּין,
chunks.en: The sword comes to the world for slowing down justice,
and for twisting justice,
and for those who teach the Torah against the halachah.

summary: This mishnah lists more punishments and their reasons, like wild animals for false oaths, and exile for the worst aveiros. It also lists the times when plague grows, because people did not give the poor what belongs to them.

chunks.en: Wild animals come to the world
for false oaths,
and for disgracing Hashem's Name.
Exile comes to the world for
those who serve idols,
and for forbidden relationships,
and for killing,
and for not letting the land rest.
At four times the plague grows:
in the fourth year, and in the seventh year,
and right after the seventh year,

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: and right after Sukkos of each and every year.

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: In the fourth year, because of maaser for the poor of the third year.
In the seventh year, because of maaser for the poor of the sixth year.
And right after the seventh year,

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: because of the fruits of the seventh year.
And right after Sukkos of each and every year,

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: because of stealing gifts of the poor.

summary: There are four kinds of people when it comes to sharing what they own. The one who says "mine is yours and yours is yours" is a chasid, and the one who says "yours is mine and mine is mine" is wicked.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of people.
One who says: Mine is mine and yours is yours,
this is an in-between way.
And some say:
this is the way of Sedom.
chunks.explain: The people of Sedom did not want to share anything.

chunks.en: Mine is yours and yours is mine:
an unlearned person.

words.note: Am ha'aretz: someone who does not understand.

chunks.en: Mine is yours and yours is yours:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי וְשֶׁלְּךָ שֶׁלִּי, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. Mine is mine and yours is mine: a wicked person.

summary: There are four kinds of tempers. Best is someone who is hard to make angry and easy to calm down; worst is someone who gets angry easily and is hard to calm down.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of tempers.
Easy to anger and easy to calm down:
his gain is lost by his loss.
Hard to anger and hard to calm down:
his loss is made up by his gain.
Hard to anger and easy to calm down:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. נוֹחַ לִכְעֹס וְקָשֶׁה לִרְצוֹת, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. Easy to anger and hard to calm down: wicked.

summary: There are four kinds of students. Best is one who learns quickly and forgets slowly; worst is one who learns slowly and forgets quickly.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of students.
Quick to understand and quick to forget:
his gain is lost by his loss.
Slow to understand and slow to forget:
his loss is made up by his gain.
Quick to understand and slow to forget:
a wise person. Slow to understand and quick to forget:
this is a bad share.

summary: There are four kinds of people who give tzedakah. Best is one who gives and wants others to give too; worst is one who does not give and does not want others to give.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of people who give tzedakah.
One who wants to give himself but does not want others to give:
he has a bad eye toward what belongs to others.
chunks.explain: He is jealous of the mitzvah others would get.

chunks.en: Others should give but he will not give:
he has a bad eye toward what is his own.
chunks.explain: He is stingy with his own money.

chunks.en: He will give and others will give:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. לֹא יִתֵּן וְלֹא יִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. He will not give and others will not give: wicked.

summary: There are four kinds of people who go to the beis midrash. Best is one who goes and also does what he learned; worst is one who neither goes nor does.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of people who go to the beis midrash.
One who goes but does not do:
he has the reward for going.
One who does but does not go:
he has the reward for doing.
One who goes and does:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. לֹא הוֹלֵךְ וְלֹא עוֹשֶׂה, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. One who does not go and does not do: wicked.

summary: There are four kinds of students who sit before the Sages: like a sponge, a funnel, a strainer and a sifter. The best is like the sifter, which keeps the good fine flour.

chunks.en: There are four kinds among those who sit before the Sages:
a sponge, and a funnel,
a strainer, and a sifter.
A sponge, which soaks up everything.
chunks.explain: He remembers everything, good and bad.

chunks.en: A funnel, which lets in on this side and lets out on that side.
chunks.explain: It goes in one ear and out the other.

chunks.he: מְשַׁמֶּרֶת, שֶׁמּוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַיַּיִן וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַשְּׁמָרִים.
chunks.en: A strainer, which lets out the wine and keeps the dregs.
chunks.explain: He keeps what is not important.

chunks.he: וְנָפָה, שֶׁמּוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַקֶּמַח וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַסֹּלֶת:
chunks.en: And a sifter, which lets out the coarse flour and keeps the fine flour.

summary: Love that depends on getting something ends when that thing is gone, but love that does not depend on anything lasts forever, like the love of Dovid and Yehonasan.

chunks.en: Any love that depends on something,
when the thing is gone,
the love is gone.
But love that does not depend on anything
is never gone.
Which love depends on something?
This is the love of Amnon and Tamar.
chunks.explain: Amnon's love was only for what he wanted, so it ended.

chunks.en: And which does not depend on anything?
This is the love of Dovid and Yehonasan.

summary: An argument for the sake of Heaven, like the arguments between Hillel and Shammai, will last. An argument not for the sake of Heaven, like that of Korach and his group, will not last.

chunks.en: Any argument that is for the sake of Heaven
will last in the end.
And one that is not for the sake of Heaven
will not last in the end.

chunks.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא מַחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
chunks.en: Which argument is for the sake of Heaven?
This is the argument of Hillel and Shammai.
And which is not for the sake of Heaven?
This is the argument of Korach and all his group.

summary: Someone who helps many people do good is protected from sin, like Moshe. Someone who makes many people sin is not given the chance to do teshuvah, like Yeravam.

chunks.en: Whoever helps the many do good,
no sin will come through him.
And whoever makes the many sin,
he is not given the chance to do teshuvah.
Moshe did good and helped the many do good,
the merit of the many is hung on him,
as it says (Devarim 33): The righteousness of Hashem
he did, and His laws with Yisrael.
Yeravam sinned and made the many sin,

words.note: A king who led many Jews to serve idols.

chunks.en: the sin of the many is hung on him,
as it says (Melachim I 15): For
the sins of Yeravam (ben Nevat) that
he sinned and that he made Yisrael sin.

summary: The students of Avraham Avinu have a good eye, a humble spirit and a soul that wants little. The students of Bilam have the opposite. Avraham's students enjoy this world and the World to Come.

chunks.en: Whoever has
these three things
is one of the students of Avraham Avinu.
And three other things,
is one of the students of Bilam the wicked.
A good eye,
and a humble spirit,
and a soul that wants little,
is one of the students of Avraham Avinu.
A bad eye,
and a proud spirit,
and a soul that wants too much,
is one of the students of Bilam the wicked.
What is the difference between the students of Avraham
Avinu and the students of Bilam the wicked?
The students of Avraham Avinu

chunks.he: אוֹכְלִין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְנוֹחֲלִין בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
chunks.en: eat in this world and inherit the World to Come,
as it says (Mishlei 8): To give an inheritance to those who love Me, there is,
and their treasure houses I will fill.
But the students of Bilam the wicked
inherit Gehinnom and go down to the deepest pit,
as it says (Tehillim 55): And You,
Hashem, will bring them down to the deepest pit,

chunks.he: אַנְשֵׁי דָמִים וּמִרְמָה לֹא יֶחֱצוּ יְמֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: men of blood and lies will not live half their days,
but I will trust in You.

summary: Yehudah ben Teima teaches to be bold like a leopard, light like an eagle, fast like a deer and strong like a lion to do what Hashem wants. He ends with a tefillah that Hashem rebuild Yerushalayim soon.

chunks.en: Yehudah ben Teima says:
Be bold like a leopard,
and light like an eagle,
and fast like a deer,
and strong like a lion,
to do the will of your Father in Heaven.
He used to say:
A bold-faced person goes to Gehinnom,
and a person who feels shame goes to Gan Eden.

chunks.he: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁתִּבְנֶה
chunks.en: May it be Your will, Hashem our G-d, that You build

chunks.he: עִירְךָ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵנוּ בְתוֹרָתֶךָ:
chunks.en: Your city soon in our days, and give us our share in Your Torah.

summary: This mishnah tells the right age for each step of life: five for Chumash, ten for Mishnah, thirteen for mitzvos, and so on, all the way to one hundred.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Five years old for Chumash,
ten for Mishnah,
thirteen for mitzvos,
fifteen for Gemara,
eighteen for the chuppah,
twenty to go after a living,
thirty for strength,
forty for understanding,
fifty for giving advice,
sixty for old age,
seventy for gray hair,
eighty for special strength,

words.note: Special strength to live so long.

chunks.en: ninety to bend over,
a hundred is as if he died
and passed and stopped from the world.

summary: Ben Bag Bag teaches in Aramaic to keep turning over the Torah again and again, because everything is in it, and there is nothing better.

chunks.en: Ben Bag Bag says:
Turn it over and turn it over,
chunks.explain: Learn the Torah again and again.

chunks.en: because everything is in it.
And look into it,
and grow old and gray in it,
and do not move away from it,
because you have no better way than it.

summary: Ben Hei Hei teaches that the reward is as big as the effort.

chunks.en: Ben Hei Hei says:
The reward is according to the effort.
